title: Issuance-Ledger / Anti-Rollback-Anchor Crash Consistency

validation.scientific_correspondence: Every frozen P19-01..P19-16 test appeared explicitly as ok in the exact frozen-head job log; the same job checked out SHA 6514f9f8530c97a3d10d4027857bfdb1b8656a8a and concluded Ran 1106 tests and OK. Workflow success alone was not used as scientific proof.

supported_bounded_claims: On the tested same-host Ubuntu/Python/SQLite/OpenSSL prototype, parent-controlled hard termination at the issuance-ledger to anti-rollback-anchor boundary did not silently convert a divergent two-store state into current authority.
A kill after issuance-ledger COMMIT but before anchor advancement remained explicitly divergent until deterministic reconciliation completed.
Fresh restart detected ledger-newer-than-anchor divergence before trusted-minimum mutation could proceed.
When the state was uniquely derivable, reconciliation advanced the authenticated anchor to the exact committed issuance binding without duplicate advancement.
Temporary anchor material written before atomic replacement was never accepted as authoritative current state.
A kill after atomic anchor replacement but before response delivery remained replay-safe and did not duplicate issuance or anchor generation.
Anchor-newer-than-ledger and conflicting same-generation states failed closed rather than being caller/model-selected.
Stale ledger and stale anchor substitutions after reconciliation were detected by retained correspondence/monotonic state in the frozen vectors.
Recovery identity semantic rebinding remained denied during divergence and after reconciliation.
Concurrent reconcilers converged on one exact authoritative anchor result in the tested same-host concurrency model.
A cryptographically valid issuance could not bypass unresolved ledger/anchor correspondence at minimum use time.
Repeated crash/restart/reconciliation preserved monotonic issuance/anchor memory and exact replay identity in the frozen sequence.
After recovery from the tested R1 to R2 divergence, a clean R2 to R3 issuance, anchor advancement and trusted-minimum advancement remained live exactly once.
Models, reviewers and ordinary registry/root/minimum surfaces gained no reconciliation-result, signer, release, deploy, production or completion authority.
explicit_nonclaims: physical power-loss or storage-controller flush guarantees
filesystem semantics across all platforms and filesystems
independent disk or storage failure domains for ledger and anchor
OS-user, host-admin, kernel or hypervisor compromise resistance
independent administrative or cloud trust domains
KMS/HSM private-key nonextractability or hardware-backed production key custody
security after joint compromise of ledger, anchor and signer key
Byzantine fault tolerance or malicious-host behavior
exhaustive interleaving coverage beyond the frozen hand-authored vectors
third-party or organizationally independent scientific adjudication
production, release, deploy or completion authority
evidence_weight_caveat: This result is strong evidence for the frozen same-host crash/reconciliation semantics, not certification of independent production trust domains. The research program preregistration, implementation and final program-level adjudication remain project-internal. External reviewer feedback has therefore been incorporated as a reason to stop automatically deepening same-host pilots and to add independent review plus systematic state-space/fault analysis before stronger claims.
retained_hygiene_debt: Pre-existing subprocess ResourceWarning messages from older governed-platform paths remain visible in the regression log and are not classified as Pilot 19 mechanism failures.
next_gap: Before opening another same-host EXP-I pilot, determine whether any remaining local boundary justifies a new hand-authored pilot or should instead be addressed by systematic state-space/fault exploration, external independent evidence review, integrated product validation, or later real KMS/multi-host trust-domain experiments.
